findings.subject: Sun Pyramid core fill materials
findings.statement: Torras Freixa reports earth mixed with tepetate volcanic tuff in the Sun Pyramid core, containing ceramics, lithic artifacts and charcoal. She cites botanical evidence indicating that some of this construction earth had previously been agricultural soil; prior agricultural use is a reported interpretation, not established direct excavation evidence from this source inspection.
findings.period: Teotihuacan monumental construction; first through early fourth centuries CE models remain contested
findings.citation: Torras Freixa 2018, ch.10 printed p.227, subsection 10.2.2; notes 575-576
findings.source_material_examined: actual original chapter printed p.227; web PDF screenshot page index 228
findings.limitations: Original 1960s excavation records and Manzanilla 2005 p.283 have not been independently read; no new fixed construction date proven.

proposed_enrichments.locator: Torras Freixa 2018 printed p.226, Figure 10.4, reproduced/modified after Sugiyama et al. 2013:409
proposed_enrichments.evidence: Pre-Sun Pyramid Structure 1 represented by a 13.5 m wall with sloping talud on both sides, aligned with Teotihuacan standard. Secondary discussion reports small obsidian offerings and a perinatal burial; their water-deity connection is hypothetical.
proposed_enrichments.warning: Do not duplicate existing canonical v94-teo-13; original 2013 plate not directly inspected; illustration reproduction © Saburo Sugiyama.
